announcements.title: Headteacher's Message: Welcome to this week’s school newsletter!
announcements.content:
Welcome to this week’s school
newsletter!

As we reach the end of another busy
and productive week at Warboys
Primary Academy, it has been
wonderful to see our children
continuing to demonstrate our school
values in everything they do. From
excellent learning in the classroom to
representing the school with pride,
there has been plenty to celebrate
across the academy.

A huge congratulations goes to all of
our

Stars of the Week

, whose hard
work, determination and positive
attitudes have deservedly been
recognised. We are also incredibly
proud of

Whales Class

for earning
their class reward after filling their
pompom jar. We hope they thoroughly
enjoy their special treat day next
week!

There are several important
reminders and upcoming events
included in this week's newsletter.
Parent Consultation appointments
are now available to book, our SEND
Coffee Morning takes place next
Wednesday with the opportunity to
meet our new Link Educational
Psychologist, and we would also
encourage families with children in
EYFS and KS1 to consider
supporting our forthcoming Diwali
Dance Workshop, which
unfortunately may need to be
cancelled if we do not receive
sufficient voluntary contributions.

We hope you enjoy reading this
week's newsletter and wish all of our
families a wonderful weekend.

announcements.title: School Reminders: Inhalers, Absences & School Dinners
announcements.content:
Important News

and Reminders

Diwali Dance Workshop -
Voluntary Contributions Needed

We are very much looking forward to
our

Diwali Dance Workshop

taking
place on

Friday 6th November 2026

for children in

EYFS and KS1

. This
exciting experience supports our RE
curriculum and will give children the
opportunity to learn about the Hindu
Festival of Lights through
storytelling, movement and dance.

Unfortunately, at present we have
received very few voluntary
contributions towards the cost of the
workshop. As these contributions
help fund the instructor leading the
sessions, we may need to

cancel the
workshop if insufficient funds are
received.

If you would like your child to benefit
from this enriching cultural
experience, we kindly ask for a
voluntary contribution of

£5.00 per
child

where possible. Payments can
be made via

Bromcom > Clubs >
Diwali Dance Workshop

, and the
payment window will remain open
until

Friday 6th November 2026.

We know the children would
thoroughly enjoy this opportunity and
we hope that, with your support, we
will be able to go ahead with the
workshops as planned. Thank you for
your continued support. 🪔✨

SEND Coffee Morning

We would like to invite parents and
carers to our

on

Wednesday 21st October from
8:30am to 9:15am.

This is a wonderful opportunity to
meet with Miss Leach and other
families in an informal setting, ask
questions, share experiences, and
find out more about the support
available for children with additional
needs.

We are also pleased to welcome our
new

Link Educational Psychologist,

who will be attending the session to
introduce herself to parents and
carers and explain more about her
role within the school. Please follow
the link to confirm whether you will
be joining us for this event

SEND
Coffee Morning - Fill in form

We look forward to seeing you there
and hope you can join us for a coffee
and a chat. ☕

Parent Consultation
Appointments

We are pleased to let parents and
carers know that

Parent Consultation
appointments are now live and
available to book

.

These meetings provide a valuable
opportunity to discuss your child's
progress, celebrate their
achievements, and talk through any
areas where they may need
additional support. We strongly
encourage all families to book an
appointment with their child's class
teacher.

Appointments can be booked via

MCAS (My Child at School)

. Please
log in to the app and select your
preferred time slot as soon as
possible, as appointments are
allocated on a first-come, first-served
basis.

If you experience any difficulties
booking your appointment, please
contact the school office for
assistance.

School Photographs

Vancols school
photographs are now available to
view and order

using the

QR code on
your proof card.

If you have already scanned the QR
code and registered, you should
receive an automatic email
notification when your photographs
are ready to view.

If you have not yet registered, don't
worry. Simply scan the QR code on
your proof card and follow the
instructions provided to access your
photographs online.

If you have not received your proof
card, or it has been misplaced, please
contact the

Vancols Parent Line on
01206 273711.

Please note that if you
do not already have a Vancols
account, you will need to contact the
school to obtain the website photo
code required to access your images.

We hope you enjoy viewing this year's
school photographs!

Cost of Living Support Update

We would like to make families aware
that the

Cambridgeshire Holiday
Voucher Scheme has now ended.

While holiday vouchers are no longer
available, a range of support
continues to be offered for families
who may be experiencing financial
difficulties.

The

Crisis and Resilience Fund

has
replaced the Household Support
Fund and is available until

31 March
2029

. Eligible families may be able to
access support with essential
household costs, and families who
previously received holiday vouchers
may be prioritised where appropriate.

We also encourage eligible families to
explore the

Holiday Activities and
Food (HAF) Programme

, which
provides free holiday activities,
healthy meals and snacks for children
during school holidays.

For further information about
available support and cost of living
assistance, please visit the
Cambridgeshire County Council
website or contact the School Office,
where we will be happy to signpost
families to additional sources of help.

Year 4 Residential Visit to
Grafham Water

We are pleased to let Year 4 parents
and carers know that

deposits are
now payable via the MCAS app

for
our exciting residential visit to

Grafham Water

, taking place from

Monday 28th June to Wednesday 30th
June 2027.

To

secure your child’s place, a non-
refundable deposit of £75

is required.
Once the deposit has been paid, the

remaining balance can be paid in
monthly instalments through MCAS.

We hope that offering the opportunity
to spread the cost over an extended
period will help make

budgeting for
the visit a little easier for families.

We are very much looking forward to
what promises to be a

fantastic and
memorable experience for our Year 4
children!

Remembrance Day – Uniformed
Organisations

As part of our

Remembrance Day
commemorations

, we would like to
invite any children who are members
of a uniformed service organisation,
such as

Scouts, Guides, Cubs,
Brownies, Cadets, St John
Ambulance

, or a similar group, to
proudly wear their

service uniform to
school on Wednesday 11th November

Children who are not members of a
uniformed organisation should attend
school in their

usual school uniform

We look forward to coming together
as a school community to mark this
important occasion and to reflect
upon and remember the sacrifices
made by those who have served, and
those who continue to serve.

Children in Need 2026 – Dress Up
and Donate!

We’re excited to support Children in
Need again this year with a fun
challenge for all pupils! On

Friday
13th November

, children are invited
to come to school dressed in
something bright, cheerful, and
smile-inducing—from Pudsey-themed
outfits to superheroes or their own
creative designs. Alongside their
joyful attire, we kindly ask for a small
donation to help raise funds for this
amazing cause, supporting children
and young people across the UK.
Let’s celebrate creativity, kindness,
and community spirit!

Win a Giant Pudsey Bear! 🐻

As part of our fundraising, we are
delighted to offer children the
exciting opportunity to

win a Giant
Pudsey Bear!

Children can enter the prize draw by
making a £1 donation per entry. On

Friday 13th November

, one number
will be selected at random and the
lucky ticket holder will take home the
Giant Pudsey Bear.

Donations can be made

online or
directly through the School Office

. We
hope lots of our children will get
involved and help us raise as much as
possible for this fantastic cause.

Thank you for your continued
generosity and support, and good luck
to all our entrants!

🐻💛

Reminder: School Gates at Drop-
Off & Collection

A polite reminder to all parents and
carers that the

Visitor Gate at the
front of the school is for visitors and
latecomers

only.

For the safety of our children and to
help keep arrival and collection times
running smoothly,

all parents and
carers dropping off or collecting
children should use the designated
side gates.

We kindly ask that you

do not use the
Visitor Gate as an entrance or exit
during normal drop-off and collection
times.

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation in helping us keep
our school site

safe, secure and well
organised.

Birthday Treats & Food in School

Following careful consideration, we
have decided that

sweets, chocolates,
cakes or other food treats should not
be brought into school to share with
classmates

, including for birthdays
and other celebrations. This is to help
us keep all children safe, particularly
those with serious or potentially life-
threatening allergies.

We also kindly remind families that

packed lunches should contain
healthy choices and must not include
sweets or chocolate

. As we operate a

nut-free approach

, please do not send
in foods containing nuts, including
peanut butter, Nutella, cereal bars
containing nuts or products labelled

“may contain nuts.”

We absolutely want children to feel
special on their birthdays! Families
are welcome to consider

non-food
alternatives

, such as stickers, small
stationery items or donating a
birthday book to the class or school
library.

Thank you for your understanding
and continued support in helping us
keep

every child safe and included.

YDP Wraparound Provision:
Booking Reminder

A reminder to parents and carers
wishing to book their child into the

wraparound provision provided by
YDP

that all bookings must be made
directly through the YDP booking
platform, which can be found

HERE

.
Please note that

YDP is a separate
provider

, and therefore the school
office is

unable to make or manage
bookings on behalf of families

Places are limited, so we strongly
encourage families to book as far in
advance as possible to avoid
disappointment.

If you need to make
a

same-day booking

, this must be
completed through the YDP booking
platform

by 1.00pm at the latest

. We
are also pleased to share that YDP
has informed us that they will be
taking on an

additional member of
staff on Tuesdays, Wednesdays and
Thursdays

, which will increase
capacity and allow

more spaces to
become available on these days

Thank you for your cooperation and
for ensuring all bookings are made
directly with YDP.

Uniform Donations

We are very grateful for all the
uniform donations we receive.
However,

we kindly ask that parents
and carers do not bring any more
uniform donations into school at this
time,

as we currently have plenty of
stock. The only items we are still able
to accept are

clean, good-condition
uniform with the school logo

,
specifically:

Jumpers and cardigans

PE tops

Hoodies

Thank you for your understanding
and continued support.

announcements.title: EEBSA-Environmental and Emotional Barriers to Scho
announcements.content:
EEBSA

-Environmental

and Emotional

Barriers to

School

Attendance

Environmental and Emotional
Barriers to School Attendance
(EEBSA) is a term used to describe a
child's difficulty attending or
engaging with school due to
emotional factors. Children may
display EEBSA in a variety of ways,
and recognising the early signs can
help ensure they receive the right
support (please see the image
provided by Cambridgeshire County
Council highlighting signs of
EEBSA).

If you have concerns that your child
may be showing signs of EEBSA,
please speak to your child's class
teacher or a member of the Senior
Leadership Team. By working
together, we can develop a shared
understanding of your child's
strengths and any barriers they may
be facing, with the aim of supporting
their wellbeing and helping them feel
happy and successful at school.

Miss Westwood

will be hosting an
informal

Coffee Afternoon on
Wednesday 18th November from
2:30pm to 3:00pm

. Parents and carers
are warmly invited to attend to find
out more about EEBSA, discuss any
concerns, and learn about the support
available.

We look forward to seeing you there.

announcements.title: Attendance Update: Termly Pizza Parties (TAPP) & Appointment Guidelines
announcements.content:
Attendance Update

Medical appointments

will continue
to be authorised only when
appointment confirmation is provided
to the school office.

Optician
appointments

will no longer be
authorised from September, as these
can usually be arranged outside
school hours.

We are also delighted to launch our

Termly Attendance Pizza Parties
(TAPP).

Pupils achieving

98%
attendance or above

each term will be
invited to a special pizza party during
the final week of term and will
receive a raffle ticket for the chance
to win a

£50 Amazon voucher.

At Warboys Primary Academy, we
know that good attendance plays a
vital role in children's academic
achievement, social development and
wellbeing. Thank you for your
continued support in helping your
child attend school regularly and
arrive on time, giving them the very
best opportunity to thrive.

Term-time leave

We appreciate that unexpected events
can happen, and we’re always here to
support families where possible.

However, Cambridgeshire County
Council and the Department for
Education require schools to
authorise leave

only in exceptional
circumstances

—meaning rare,
unavoidable events.

Routine family holidays or planned
trips unfortunately do not meet this
threshold. You can find further
information here:

Non-attendance at school and the
law | Cambridgeshire County
Council

Thank you for your understanding
and cooperation.

announcements.title: Young Carers: Support & Parent Concern Form
announcements.content:
At our school, we are proud to
support our Young Carers and
recognise the important role they
play within their families. We work
closely with Centre 33 to provide
external support, while internally we
offer fortnightly Young Carers
sessions where children can come
together to chat, share experiences,
take part in activities, and relax in a
supportive environment. Led by Miss
Coles and Mrs Flisher, with support
from Mr Bostock, these sessions help
ensure our Young Carers feel valued,
understood, and supported. We are
also committed to raising awareness
across the school community and
celebrating the dedication, resilience,
and compassion shown by our Young
Carers every day.

Please follow the link below to flag
any child that you may deem to be a
Young Carer. A Young Carer is a
child young person who helps to look
after a family member who may have
an illness, disability, mental health
difficulty, or who may need extra
support for another reason. This care
can include practical tasks, emotional
support, or helping siblings, and it
may take place before or after the
school day. We recognise that these
responsibilities can sometimes impact
a child’s wellbeing, learning, and
emotional needs. All conversations
and responses will be treated
sensitively and in confidence.

Fill in form

announcements.title: P.T.F.A: Pre-Loved School Uniform Sales
announcements.content:
A Word from the

P.T.F.A

💛 Could you help keep our PTFA
going?

Our PTFA is a wonderful part of the
Warboys Primary Academy
community, helping to bring exciting
events and opportunities to our
children while raising much-needed
funds for the school. However,

we
urgently need more parents and carers
to get involved.

Following several of our valued
committee members stepping down
as their children finished at the
school last year, we are now facing a
very real challenge.

We are losing our
Treasurer, along with other
experienced members, and without
enough people willing to step forward,
we may have no choice but to fold the
PTFA.

We really don't want that to happen.
You might think you need lots of free
time or previous experience to join
the PTFA,

you don't!

We need people
who can help in whatever way they
can. That could mean helping at an
event, coming along with ideas,
taking on a committee role, helping
with fundraising, or simply lending a
hand occasionally.

Every person who gets involved
makes the workload lighter for
everyone else — and helps us
continue providing those extra
experiences and opportunities
for our children.

💛

Pre‑Loved School Uniform

A quick reminder that our PTFA sell
high‑quality

pre‑loved uniform

through their Facebook page. It’s a
great way to save money, support the
school, and give uniform items a new
life.Please check out their page if you
need any extra bits for the term

HERE.
